clue.text: Be afraid to belch

definitions.meaning: to become nervous or frightened, an informal idiom
to bring up air from the stomach, as one does when burping a baby

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for growing scared, and taken literally it describes raising gas from the stomach.

clue.text: George North captured everything which carried Spanish gold

indicators.note: something captured is held inside a captor, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Geo. is the old written abbreviation of the name George
everything means all
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A man called George, up north, seized everything aboard a treasure ship from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured' puts ALL inside GEO + N, after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sailing warship of the sixteenth century, famous for ferrying American treasure back to Spain.

clue.text: Boring way to make hay with letters of credit

parts.note: to ted is to spread out cut grass so it dries into hay
IOUs are written promises to pay, notes acknowledging a debt

explanation.surface: Haymaking described in terms of credit notes sounds a dull affair.
explanation.walkthrough: TED is a farming verb meaning to turn and spread mown grass for drying.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something dull and wearisome, a plain synonym.

clue.text: He may send people off with a wave of the hand

definitions.text: He may send people off with a wave of the hand

parts.words: He may send people off with a wave of the hand
parts.note: reads like someone dismissing visitors with a gesture, but describes a performer putting subjects into a trance with a pass of the hand

explanation.definitionFit: A stage mesmerist sends subjects off to sleep with gestures, the 'send off' being into a trance.

clue.text: West to declare positively yet sway first this way then that

definitions.text: sway first this way then that

parts.note: W is the compass abbreviation for west
to aver is to state firmly as fact

explanation.surface: A Westerner who speaks with conviction still vacillates.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate or oscillate, moving unsteadily from side to side.

clue.text: Unable to distinguish art from tart?

definitions.text: Unable to distinguish art from tart?

parts.words: Unable to distinguish art from tart?
parts.note: suggests someone with poor judgement in culture or morals, while also hinting that 'art' and 'tart' differ only by one letter

explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking discernment in aesthetic matters is said to have none of this quality.

clue.text: Call on the suet pudding about 1.51

indicators.note: one set of letters goes about, or around, the other
a pudding is a mixture, so the letters of suet are mixed up

parts.note: in Roman numerals 1 is I and 51 is LI

explanation.surface: Turn to the suet pudding at around nine minutes to two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pudding' scrambles SUET to UTSE, and 'about' puts it round ILI, from 1 and 51 in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on resources is to make use of or employ them.

clue.text: Speciously concealing faults guaranteed by soap-powder ads

definitions.meaning: glossing over wrongdoing with a misleading show
laundry detergent adverts promise brilliantly clean, bright laundry

explanation.definitionFit: Covering up scandal is a metaphorical cover of pale paint, while detergent commercials literally promise snowy laundry.

clue.text: Hiding from hold-up so one hears

indicators.note: tells us the word is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: a robbery or a delay

explanation.surface: Concealing oneself after a robbery, according to what one is told.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low somewhere is to be hiding out, sheltering in a refuge.

clue.text: Acid used by six before 3.50

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second in the answer

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a three is a trio, and 50 is L in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A corrosive used by half a dozen people shortly before ten to four.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil of vitriol is an old name for sulphuric acid, a corrosive chemical.

clue.text: Escapist literature suitable for illuminated manuscripts?

definitions.meaning: illuminated suggests lit up, so such manuscripts would offer bright pages to read

explanation.definitionFit: Easy fiction is undemanding fare, and a manuscript glowing with illumination would be bright to read.

clue.text: Lot more variation in voice!

indicators.note: a variation alters the order, so the letters of lot more are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer exclaims at the extra wobble in a voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A wavering, trembling effect in singing is a quivering vibrato-like ornament.

clue.text: Making haste to wrap heavy blanket around exposed part of leg

indicators.note: wrapping puts one thing round another, so a piece goes inside
one piece sits around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a rug is a thick blanket or travelling throw
the shin is the front of the lower leg, often bare and easily knocked

explanation.surface: Hurrying to cover a bare shin with a thick rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wrap' and 'around' put SHIN inside RUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurrying or dashing, moving in great haste.

clue.text: Staffs to conjure with

parts.note: Staffs suggests the county abbreviation or employees, but means rods used by magicians

explanation.definitionFit: Magicians wave slender sticks when performing spells or tricks.

clue.text: Carry out a piece of equipment

definitions.meaning: to put a plan into effect

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to execute a plan; as a noun it is a tool.

clue.text: Someone Len put up for the staff

parts.note: someone means a person

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up a word means reading it upwards, backwards

parts.note: a man's name taken as written

explanation.surface: Somebody named Len was nominated for the workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: The employees of an organisation collectively, its workforce.

clue.text: Butcher displaying singular merriment

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
merriment shows itself in laughter

explanation.surface: A butcher with a uniquely cheerful manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher is to kill brutally or in great numbers, as a verb synonym.

clue.text: A superior accomplice

parts.note: superior means better

explanation.surface: An accomplice who outranks the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: One who encourages or assists a crime, as in aiding and abetting.

clue.text: Cowardly as a fiddler with no strings to pull

definitions.text: as a fiddler with no strings to pull
definitions.meaning: violin strings were traditionally made of catgut, so a fiddler without them lacks gut

explanation.definitionFit: Lacking nerve, and literally without catgut strings for a violin.

clue.text: The serviceman's serviceman

parts.note: a man who conducts religious services for soldiers, sailors and airmen

explanation.definitionFit: A military chaplain holds church services for those in the armed forces.

clue.text: State of Louisiana having an enormous bill for fish

definitions.text: State of Louisiana having an enormous bill for fish

parts.words: State of Louisiana having an enormous bill for fish
parts.note: suggests a huge invoice for seafood, but describes a big-beaked bird; Louisiana is nicknamed after the bird

explanation.definitionFit: A waterbird with a huge pouched beak for scooping prey, emblem of Louisiana's state nickname.

clue.text: US serviceman turns up in uniform to change the subject

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: dress is formal military uniform, as in full dress

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier appears in uniform to move the conversation on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' makes IG, which 'in' places within DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander off the point in speech or writing, a synonym.

clue.text: I retain a disposition to stay put

definitions.text: I retain a disposition to stay put

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters of I retain are set out anew

explanation.surface: Someone admits to a reluctance to move.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, a body's tendency to remain at rest; generally, sluggish resistance to change.

clue.text: Passageway from a small piece of land

parts.note: an isle is a small island

explanation.surface: A corridor leading off a little plot of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkway between rows of seats, as in a church or aircraft.

clue.text: Did a favour by arranging big dole

indicators.note: arranging puts things in a new order, so the letters of big dole are reordered

explanation.surface: Helped someone out by organising a generous handout.
explanation.definitionFit: To accommodate or help someone, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Collects and takes in dresses

definitions.meaning: in sewing, puckering fabric by drawing a thread through it

explanation.definitionFit: It means amasses, and in dressmaking it means drawing fabric into small folds.

clue.text: No uncle ordered this little scrap

indicators.note: ordered means put in order, so the letters of no uncle are rearranged

explanation.surface: Without an uncle around, a small quarrel is begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' suggests a fight; here it is a tiny particle.
explanation.definitionFit: A proton or neutron, a minute particle within the atomic core.

clue.text: Disobeyed railway track notice leading to misunderstanding

definitions.meaning: went over the rails despite warning signs not to cross

explanation.definitionFit: Literally stepping over the rails; idiomatically a telephone fault or confusion where people talk at cross purposes.
